annotations.title: Check a GitHub Actions workflow for script injection

description:
Checks the text of one GitHub Actions workflow file for script injection: places where text an outside user controls (an issue or pull request title or body, a comment, a branch name, a commit message) is pasted into a shell script or a github-script body, a privileged trigger that checks out a pull request's code, event text re-evaluated through eval, an externally triggerable workflow with open token permissions, and an AI agent action on such a trigger. Built from Radware's 2026-10-29 report of 83 hidden-command attacks on 61 public repositories.

Static and local: nothing is fetched, run or stored. Pass the workflow's YAML as text (max 28000 characters; use the DugganUSA Checks GitHub Action for whole repositories). Returns {verdict:"block"|"review"|"advisory"|"no-findings"|"unknown", findings:[{rule, severity, verdict, line, expression, message, fix}], coverage, note}. "no-findings" means none of the listed patterns were seen; it does NOT mean the workflow is safe. "unknown" means nothing was analyzed.

One tool call, no auth.

workflow.description: The workflow file text (the YAML of a file under .github/workflows).
